title: How small can a face or a person be before a real detector stops finding it?
summary: Measured recall against pixel size for real detectors on COCO photos, replacing the assumed curve in capture-bystander. 22 confident faces and 254 labelled people from 128 photos were shrunk by scales from 1 to 0.065 and each detector asked to find them again. YuNet at its usual 0.6 score found every face of 16 px or wider and half at 10 px (fitted 50% point 9.2 px, range 8.2–10.4), not the assumed 20; at a 0.9 threshold it is 26.6 px. On an 8K 360 camera the per-frame leak among faces of at least 32 px falls from the assumed 4.8% to 0.01% (36% to 0.9% at 16 px), and rises to 7.2% at the 0.9 threshold. A YOLOX-s person detector reaches 52% at 20–32 px of height and 94% at 96–128 px (50% point 23 px, not 40); the head sits in the top quarter to third of its box. Section F: by how far the face is turned from the camera, YuNet at 0.9 falls from 54% to 16% recall (54 faces) and the frontal Haar cascade from 66% to 16%, while YuNet at 0.6 holds 95%+; the turn is a landmark proxy and back-of-head is not covered. A pilot: the reference faces are easy by construction (frontal, confident), the photos are shrunk not distant, and n is small, so these are optimistic bounds; the identifiable size is still assumed.
lede: how small can a face be before a real detector misses it? YuNet found every face of 16 px or wider and half at 10 px (assumed: 20), cutting the modelled blur leak on an 8K 360 camera from 4.8% to 0.01%; YOLOX finds half of people at 23 px tall. A pilot on 22 easy faces in 128 COCO photos: an optimistic bound.
